newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Meristem sees flat H1 profits.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Meristem sees flat H1 profits.

text.p: Chemicals and minerals group Meristem Plc said on Tuesday that it expected profits in the first half of 1997 to be flat before picking up in the second half.
In a telephone interview with Reuters, chief executive Donald Neil said the first two months of 1997 had started "slowly," and he did not "expect any growth in first half profits."
Neil said a strong performance in processed minerals in the first half of 1996 and rapid growth last year by the E Wood coatings business would be difficult to match.
"Sales were strong last year in processed minerals and that has not been quite so strong this year," said Neil. The division posted operating profits of 2.1 milion stg on sales of 11 million stg.

He said growth at E Wood, in its first full year as part of Meristem, "was dramatic," with operating profits more than trebling to 1.74 million stg on sales of 10.7 million. Neil said it would not be realistic "to expect a similar level of growth in this forthcoming 12 months."
He said the strength of sterling would also have an impact on Meristem, which exports a substantial portion of output.

With group pre-tax profit up 25 percent last year to 3.6 million stg on sales up 80 percent at 30.14 million stg, Neil said "we have demonstrated that all three businesses are capable of growing and eminently capable of further organic growth in future."

Neil said he was "quite satisifed" with the group's three main businesses, which also include the formulated chemicals arm Solvitol, and would not diversify much further from this core through acquisitions.

He said Solvitol's profit margins of 7.6 percent were well below the 15 to 20 percnt margins the business was capable of. He said that in the the next two years he wanted to see Solvitol's margins "well into double figures."
Shares in Meristem, which was formerly known as MTM, closed down 15-1/2 pence at 74 pence.
The company's founder and former chairman Richard Lines was sentenced to two years in prison last month, after being found guilty of false accounting and making misleading statements.
